niche: Psychology & human behavior (biases, habits, social dynamics)

ideas.title: Why Your Brain Can't Forget Unfinished Tasks
ideas.angle: The video explains the Zeigarnik Effect, where the brain prioritizes incomplete tasks, and reveals a simple 'shutdown' trick to stop overthinking at night.

hook.en: You can't stop thinking about it.
hook.fr: Tu n'arrives pas à arrêter d'y penser.

ideas.reason: Brain-hack content is currently peaking on Shorts with users seeking relief from burnout and mental clutter. The Zeigarnik Effect provides a scientific explanation for a universal frustration.
sources: Zeigarnik, B. (1927). Über das Behalten von erledigten und unerledigten Handlungen.
American Psychological Association - The Zeigarnik Effect

ideas.title: Why Being Clumsy Makes You More Likable
ideas.angle: It reveals the 'Pratfall Effect,' showing that highly competent people become more attractive and relatable when they make a small mistake, challenging the pressure to be perfect.
ideas.reason: Social anxiety and 'perfectionism' are trending topics among Gen Z and Millennials. This counter-intuitive advice provides instant relief and a shareable 'aha' moment.
sources: Aronson, E., Willerman, B., & Floyd, J. (1966). The effect of a pratfall on increasing interpersonal attractiveness.

ideas.title: Why Having Too Many Options Is Ruining Your Life
ideas.angle: Based on the 'Jam Study,' the video shows how choice overload leads to decision paralysis and less satisfaction, explaining why we struggle with Netflix or menus.

hook.en: Too many choices are making you miserable.
hook.fr: Trop de choix te rend malheureux.

ideas.reason: Decision fatigue is a major talking point in modern lifestyle minimalism. Relatable examples like 'choosing a movie' create high retention and comment engagement.
sources: Iyengar, S. S., & Lepper, M. R. (2000). When choice is demotivating.
The Paradox of Choice - Barry Schwartz
